visual: Ultramarine-blue lacecaps · deep purple-black stems · dark-green leaves
soilWarning: Avoid dry soil · shelter from cold winds
prune: Prune Group 4; remove faded flowers and oldest stems in spring
toxicity: Skin allergen · harmful if eaten by dogs and cats
hardinessNote: RHS H5; flowers can be affected by late frosts
uses: containers · shrub borders · cut flowers · woodland gardens
uncertain: Flower colour varies with soil pH and aluminium availability, ranging from blue-violet to pink; blue is the characteristic acid-soil form
RHS records the cultivar as a vigorous rounded-upright shrub and gives 1–1.5 m height and spread; specialist sources report it can reach about 1.5–2 m
Current RHS records 'Zorro' as PBR protected and an AGM cultivar; the original cultivar was selected by André van Zoest and is a branch sport of 'Blaumeise'
